## Instagram

**Platform:** Instagram (image post)  
**Caption:**

Bird droppings aren't just gross. They're acid.

pH 3.5–4.5 — closer to vinegar than rainwater.

In Melbourne winter, they don't dry out and flake off. Rain spreads them across your panels. Cold temperatures extend how long they sit. Etching can begin within 48 hours.

The result: a faint shadow baked into your clear coat that doesn't wash out. It polishes out — or if it's deep enough, it resprays out.

Ceramic coating stops this before it starts. Droppings land on the coating, not your paint. Wipe off clean, no contact with the clear coat.

If you're not coated yet — damp microfibre, press and lift, never wipe. And book your ceramic consultation via the link in bio.

## Facebook

**Platform:** Facebook  
**Caption:**

If your car's been parked under trees in South Yarra or along the Esplanade in Brighton this winter, there's a good chance bird droppings have already started working on your paint.

At pH 3.5–4.5, they etch into clear coat faster than most people realise — especially when Melbourne rain spreads them across panels instead of washing them away cleanly. The damage often isn't obvious until you're under a detail light in direct sun: a faint dull shadow baked into the clear coat that won't wash or wipe out.

Ceramic coating stops this at the source. Droppings land on the coating, not your paint, and wipe off clean. If you're not coated yet, the short-term answer is simple: damp microfibre, press and lift, don't wipe. The long-term answer is a coating that prevents the contact altogether.

We come to you — your driveway, office car park, or building in the CBD. Book online or tag a mate whose car needs some protection this winter.

## LinkedIn

**Platform:** LinkedIn  
**Caption:**

Here's what most car owners get wrong about Melbourne winters: the threat to your paint doesn't take a break.

Bird droppings are acidic at pH 3.5–4.5 — and they cause more etching damage in winter than summer because they don't dry out and fall off cleanly. Melbourne rain distributes them across panels. Cold temperatures extend exposure time. By the time the damage is visible — a dull shadow on the bonnet or roof — the clear coat has already been compromised.

For professionals driving $60K–$200K vehicles, this has real financial consequences. Clear coat damage that reaches primer means panel respray territory — typically $800–$2,000 per panel, and it shows at trade-in time. It's not a cosmetic problem; it's an asset value problem.

Ceramic coating creates a chemical barrier bonded to your clear coat. Droppings land on the ceramic layer and wipe off without contacting the paint beneath. One application, manufacturer-backed for up to 8 years, applied at your home, office car park, or building — no workshop drop-off, no arranging transport. Winter is actually the right time to apply it: the coating cures in controlled temperatures, and you'll be protected heading into a Melbourne spring — UV season, pollen, and all.

If you're running a late-model European or prestige vehicle and haven't had a ceramic applied, now's the window. DM us or comment below and we'll outline what the right protection looks like for your specific vehicle.
